messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT - PagerDuty PD-8921 fired for service=redwood-inference-runtime (P1) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: symptom=CUDA allocation failure / kernel OOM on host gpu-serve-07, region=eu-west-1, affected_pool=serving-prod-eu; recent logs show repeated 'cudaMalloc' failures and driver OOMs. link=https://pagerduty.example/PD-8921

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-8921 assigned to schedule 'eng-oncall-eu'. Escalation policy will notify second oncall in 5m if unacked.

Aisha: acked PD-8921 :white_check_mark:  I'm on it. Initial ask: is this isolated to this node or multiple hosts?

Ben: looking at metrics now. gpu-serve-07 shows abrupt VRAM jump from 3.2GB->23.9GB at 12:04:11 UTC, mem.free dropping to 0. Evictions spiked. kubernetes pods on that node: inference-worker:replica-12 (pid 2048) hogging memory.

Carlos: requesting dmesg and driver logs. If anyone can paste the last kernel OOM lines.

Ben: dmesg snippet:
```
[Mar 15 12:04:12] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1c.0): 61, pid=2048, GPU memory access fault
[Mar 15 12:04:12] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2048 (inference-worker) score 200 or sacrifice child
[Mar 15 12:04:12] kernel: Killed process 2048 (inference-worker) total-vm: 24576000kB, anon-rss: 24500000kB
```

Aisha: ok. plan: 1) drain node to stop new inferences 2) reroute traffic off serving-prod-eu pool (canary) 3) restart inference-worker after collecting core/logs. Doing step 1 now.

Aisha: run: `kubectl cordon gpu-serve-07 && kubectl drain gpu-serve-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`

Ben: drain started, but eviction blocked by a pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff (inference-worker-12). Trying `kubectl delete pod inference-worker-12 --grace-period=0 --force` to force remove.

sre-bot: Autoscaling action: launched 2 replacement gpu nodes in eu-west-1 (type gpus-rt-2xA100). New nodes registering; routing will shift as they become healthy.

Carlos: hypothesis: kvcache growth + long-running generation requests caused uncontrollable KV growth; suspect memory leak in LRU eviction path. Suggest lowering runtime.kv_cache.max_bytes and enabling aggressive prefix cache eviction until we patch.

Carlos: proposed runtime config patch (applying to serving-prod-eu):
```
runtime:
  kv_cache:
    enabled: true
    max_bytes: 1073741824  # 1 GiB (was 8 GiB)
    eviction_policy: aggressive
```

Aisha: applying config change to canary subset (10% traffic) now via: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/configs/apply -d '{"target":"serving-prod-eu/canary","patch":"kv_cache.max_bytes=1g"}'`

support-engineer: support ticket S-4532: customers A: acme-eu, B: mediato-eu, C: research-co reported latency spikes and failed requests between 12:03-12:10 UTC. No evidence of data corruption; only inference timeouts. Marking as impacted.

Ben: forced pod delete succeeded; inference-worker restarted on the node but reconsumed large memory during bootstrap - restarting into drained state to avoid serving. Logs show repeated cache warm-up allocations.

Aisha: switching routing: reducing serving-prod-eu weight by 30% and sending to fallback-model-1 for large requests to reduce memory pressure. Command: `rb-routing set-weight --pool serving-prod-eu --weight 70` then `rb-routing set-weight --pool fallback-model-1 --weight +30`

Ben: after traffic shift, memory on gpu-serve-07 trending down. New nodes registered and started taking traffic. kube node memory usage now 6GB free.

sre-bot: Incident automation: created incident-runbook ticket IR-8921 with steps taken and logs attached. Also scheduled a post-incident fuzz test for kv cache path.

Carlos: pushed runtime patch to infra branch: reduce kv cache + add additional guard for max allocation per-request. Will roll to serving-prod-eu once canary runs 15m without regressions.

Aisha: customer impact summary for status page:
- Region: EU-West-1
- Window: 12:03 - 12:16 UTC (mitigations ongoing)
- Impact: increased latency and ~2% failed requests for 3 customers (acme-eu, mediato-eu, research-co) using large-context generation.
- No data exposure.

Ben: manual restart of inference-worker on gpu-serve-07 completed at 12:18 UTC, memory stable. Observability: token generation latency returning to normal.

support-engineer: notified affected customers with ETA: monitoring for 1 hour and will follow up.

Aisha: marking PD-8921 as acknowledged -> will keep this thread open for handoff. Monitoring window 30m.

Maya: I'm next oncall starting 03:00 UTC. I will pick up at handoff: will watch the OOM metric and GPU alloc failure counts; if PD re-fires escalate to platform lead.

Aisha: handoff notes -> check `kernel.oops` and `runtime.kv_cache.evictions` graphs, check `inference-worker` rss per pid, and confirm canary `kv_cache.max_bytes=1g` is stable.

Carlos: exception: we found one repeatable repro on a synthetic prompt that warms kv cache beyond expected; creating follow-up bug RB-1764.

incident-bot: PD-8921 status changed: acknowledged at 1768901290 by Aisha.

incident-bot: PD-8921 resolved at 1768901449 (condition: error rate back to baseline, node healthy).

Aisha: closing thread for now. Will reopen if PD re-triggers. Thanks team :thumbsup:
